answer: Divergent-Challenge Sampling: each identity is periodically asked to solve a fresh random task derived from its own accumulated history, and answers are committed before the challenge seed is revealed. A clone sharing the same history cannot produce divergent answers without splitting from its origin, so coordinated copies fail. Cost per identity: one full history replay plus a unique response, rising toward a zenith as history grows. Attacker pays linear storage and compute per copy, with no ember of shared work reusable and only umber margins left.
